---
title: "Bibliography and External Readings"
subtitle: "Sources used to shape the technical, pedagogical, and ethical design of this course"
---

This page records the sources that informed the course architecture, explanations, examples, and tooling. The business scenarios and synthetic datasets in this site are original teaching materials; the links below provide the conceptual and technical foundations we used while building them.

## R and tidyverse foundations

- **[R for Data Science, 2e](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/)** — Hadley Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel, and Garrett Grolemund. The primary curriculum model for workflow, transformation, visualization, exploration, and communication.
- **[R Language Definition](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-lang.html)** — The official reference for R's evaluation model, objects, environments, functions, and control structures.
- **[R Documentation](https://www.rdocumentation.org/)** — A searchable index used to check package functions and example signatures.
- **[dplyr reference](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/)** — Official documentation for filtering, selecting, mutating, grouping, summarizing, arranging, and joining data.
- **[tidyr reference](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/)** — Official documentation for tidy data and `pivot_longer()`/`pivot_wider()` reshaping.
- **[ggplot2 reference](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/)** — Official documentation for the Grammar of Graphics, layers, scales, themes, and statistical transformations.
- **[scales reference](https://scales.r-lib.org/)** — Documentation for readable currency, percentage, date, and number formatting.

## Interactive publishing and reproducibility

- **[Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/)** — Project configuration, websites, executable documents, publishing, and cross-format authoring.
- **[Shinylive for R](https://posit-dev.github.io/r-shinylive/)** — Client-side WebAssembly execution for Shiny applications without a backend R server.
- **[Shinylive Quarto extension](https://quarto-ext.github.io/shinylive/)** — The extension and filter used for the live `{shinylive-r}` blocks in this site.
- **[GitHub Pages documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pages)** — Hosting and deployment context for the published course site.

## AI-assisted programming and responsible use

- **[OpenAI Codex documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex)** — Product and workflow documentation consulted for repository-aware AI coding tasks.
- **[GitHub Copilot documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot)** — Reference for editor-based AI assistance, suggestions, and responsible use.
- **[Anthropic Claude documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/)** — Reference for conversational coding and context-window practices.
- **[NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework)** — A governance reference that informed the course emphasis on validity, transparency, privacy, and accountability.
- **[NIST Generative AI Profile](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework/ai-rmf-generative-ai-profile)** — A companion reference for risks specific to generative systems, including confabulation and human oversight.

## Design references

- **[EECS 280 course materials](https://eecs280staff.github.io/eecs280.org/)** — The course architecture was inspired by the public-facing structure of a rigorous programming course: clear prerequisites, milestones, project specifications, grading expectations, and reproducibility standards. This site does not reproduce EECS 280 assignments or proprietary materials.
- **[Tidy Data](https://vita.had.co.nz/papers/tidy-data.html)** — Hadley Wickham's paper describing the principles behind tidy data and why consistent structure makes analysis easier to compose.

## How to cite this site

For a course project, cite the page and the underlying source that informed the method. For example: “The pipeline follows the tidy data and transformation conventions described in R4DS, with the business scenario and synthetic data supplied by *Intro to R for Business Analytics*.” Include the date accessed for web documentation when your institution requires it.
